requirements.requirement: On node1, datauser is limited to 100 MB of storage under /srv/data through filesystem-native enforcement.
requirements.summary: A dedicated XFS filesystem is mounted at /srv/data with user quotas enabled. XFS reports accounting and enforcement ON and 100M soft and hard limits for datauser. A 110 MiB write was rejected with “Disk quota exceeded” at the quota boundary. After restart, the mount and limits recovered and another over-limit write was rejected.

requirements.requirement: Retain the installed operating-system release and kernel and use software compatible with the legacy platform.
requirements.summary: AlmaLinux 9.6 and kernel 5.14.0-570.12.1.el9_6.x86_64 were unchanged before and after execution and restart. The solution uses functioning platform-native XFS quota facilities, with package health remaining clean.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied. Filesystem-enforced XFS quota behavior was demonstrated before and after restart, and the operating-system release and kernel were retained. The provider restart protocol is complete: healthy pre-restart state and boot identity were captured, restart was acknowledged, the boot identity changed, and service, quota, data, and system health recovered; lifecycle boot observations independently corroborate the transition.

operational_hygiene.summary: No unnecessary mutations were identified. Account, directory, backing filesystem, fstab entry, mount, permissions, and quota changes directly implement the requested outcome. Temporary quota-test files were bounded evidence and removed. The retained sentinel supported mandatory restart recovery verification. The restart was required by the provider protocol. Final observations show no failed services, new network exposure, package damage, or abandoned temporary files.
